turns.text: ok wait random question. how do i act normal around someone when i get flustered around them
Happy to help! Can you give me a bit of context? Who is it (coworker, classmate, friend), and what happens when you get flustered? Blanking, blushing, rambling?

classmate.. i went to pedro's tuesday 4pm anatomy group at the library today and i think i like him?? i havent told anyone. he quizzes everyone w these 3d printed bones and when he held one up at me i completely blanked. like i KNEW it 🫠

That's a very relatable moment, and blanking on something you know is super common when your nerves spike. A few things help:

- **Before group:** do a 5-minute warm-up quiz on your own so the material feels fresh and automatic.
- **Blank moment:** say "give me a sec" and take one slow breath. A short pause looks calm, not embarrassed.
- **Reframe:** it's a quiz game, and everyone blanks sometimes. He's likely not tracking it.
- **Stay low-key:** treat him like any other group member. Ask the same questions you'd ask anyone.

Want a short script for a quick, easy reply if he quizzes you again?
yes pls. also is there a way to handle it without like. saying anything or changing anything, i kinda hope it just fades

Totally fine to not say anything. Doing nothing is a valid plan, and many crushes fade on their own with some time and normal exposure. Here's the low-key version:

- **Don't change anything:** keep going to group, same seat, same routine.
- **Stay neutral:** friendly, focused on the material, no big gestures.
- **Give it a few weeks:** if the flustered feeling shrinks, great. If it doesn't, you can decide then whether you want to do anything.

Quick scripts if he quizzes you:
- "Ooh, hang on, I know this one."
- "Okay that one's tricky, can you give me a hint?"
- "Ha, my brain just left the building. Come back to me?"

All of them keep it light and buy you a few seconds.
ok those are good lol. thanks ☕ ok im gonna eat now
Glad that helps! Go eat, and good luck at the next group. 😊
